fact: The World Bank restructuring paper says the Madagascar government's DECIM project is preparing the first batch of about a hundred cell towers to extend rural connectivity, with ARTEC drafting tenders for launch by end of June 2024, and a feasibility study for expanding rural digital connectivity at evaluation stage.
system: Digital and Energy Connectivity for Inclusion in Madagascar Project (DECIM)

fact: The Digital Development Minister says the government's telecom expansion programme targets 108 districts, 935 communes and 3,844 fokontany, prioritising locations with no or limited network, with rollout dependent on funding.
The Digital Development Minister says the government has already implemented solutions in 146 fokontany under its telecom expansion programme.
Connecting Africa says the government's Digital and Energy Connectivity for Inclusion in Madagascar (DECIM) project, launched in 2023, focuses on deploying infrastructure in underserved areas.
Minister Delmotte says she launched a USD 55 million subsidy under the World Bank-financed DECIM project to connect remote areas through private-sector towers, fibre and network expansion.

Minister Stephanie Delmotte announced on 31 July 2025 a government network extension project in Menabe region with Yas Madagascar and Huawei, to equip 73 pilot sites with RuralStar towers to extend 4G and reduce the digital divide.
